data.description: A rare benign primary cardiac tumor composed of fibroblasts and abundant collagen, usually arising within ventricular myocardium in infants or children. It is typically a firm, well-circumscribed intramyocardial mass.
symptoms_in_common: Prenatally detected solid cardiac mass
Well-defined mass involving or adjacent to ventricular myocardium on fetal MRI and echocardiography
Gross firm pale-tan mass
Histology showing spindle-shaped cells within abundant collagenous/fibrous stroma
Trichrome staining highlighting prominent collagen
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as arrhythmia, ventricular outflow obstruction, heart failure, or sudden cardiac events were provided

data.description: A benign myofibroblastic tumor that may occur congenitally and can rarely involve the heart. Histology commonly shows spindle-cell proliferation, collagen, and branching thin-walled vascular channels.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital/prenatal presentation
Solitary solid cardiac mass
Spindle-cell proliferation on histology
Prominent small vascular channels within the lesion
Collagenous stroma
symptoms_not_in_common: No multifocal skin, bone, soft-tissue, or visceral lesions were described
No clinical evidence of systemic infantile myofibromatosis was provided

data.description: The most common fetal and pediatric cardiac tumor, usually a benign hamartomatous lesion of cardiac muscle. It is strongly associated with tuberous sclerosis complex and often regresses after birth.
symptoms_in_common: Fetal cardiac mass detected by prenatal imaging
Potential intramyocardial ventricular location
May be asymptomatic prenatally
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears to have collagen-rich spindle-cell histology rather than the large vacuolated 'spider cells' typical of rhabdomyoma
A single lesion is described rather than multiple intramyocardial nodules
No findings suggestive of tuberous sclerosis complex were provided

data.description: A rare benign vascular tumor of the heart that can arise in the myocardium, endocardium, or pericardium. It consists of proliferating vascular channels and may be detected incidentally or prenatally.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac mass identified on imaging
Vascular channels seen histologically
Potentially well-circumscribed lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is predominantly fibrous and collagenous rather than composed mainly of dilated blood-filled vascular spaces
The gross specimen is not described as dark red-blue, hemorrhagic, or spongy
No imaging evidence of marked vascular flow or enhancement was provided

data.diagnosis: Acute pyelonephritis with focal bacterial nephritis
data.description: Acute bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma; focal bacterial nephritis is a localized, non-liquefactive inflammatory renal mass that can appear wedge-shaped or mass-like on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Focal wedge-shaped or poorly defined abnormal renal parenchymal regions on ultrasound and MRI
Altered renal cortical echogenicity and heterogeneous renal appearance
Reduced or abnormal intrarenal vascularity on Doppler imaging
Possible perinephric inflammatory change/edema on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, flank pain, dysuria, pyuria, or positive urine culture is provided
No stated history of recurrent urinary infection or urinary obstruction

data.description: Renal infarction is ischemic necrosis of renal tissue caused by occlusion of a renal arterial branch or the main renal artery, often producing peripheral wedge-shaped lesions and absent perfusion.
symptoms_in_common: Wedge-shaped peripheral renal parenchymal abnormalities
Areas with reduced or absent Doppler perfusion
MRI appearance compatible with segmental ischemic renal involvement
Possible vascular abnormality near the renal hilum
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute severe flank pain is reported
No hematuria, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, atrial fibrillation, embolic source, or hypercoagulable condition is provided
No explicit arterial occlusion or nonenhancement is described in the case text

data.description: A renal abscess is a localized collection of pus within the kidney, usually developing as a complication of ascending pyelonephritis or hematogenous bacterial spread.
symptoms_in_common: Focal renal lesion with heterogeneous ultrasound appearance
Abnormal focal renal signal on MRI
Potential reduced central vascularity in an infected focal lesion
Possible surrounding inflammatory changes
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly described fluid collection, cavity, internal debris, or rim-enhancing lesion
No fever, bacteremia, leukocytosis, or persistent infection symptoms are provided
The wedge-shaped appearance is more suggestive of pyelonephritis or infarction than a mature abscess

data.description: Renal vein thrombosis is clot formation in the renal venous drainage, which may cause renal enlargement, parenchymal edema, reduced venous flow, hematuria, and impaired renal function.
symptoms_in_common: Possible hilar vascular abnormality on MRI
Abnormal renal parenchymal appearance that may reflect edema or venous congestion
Altered intrarenal Doppler vascular pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite renal vein thrombus or absent venous flow is explicitly stated
No hematuria, acute kidney injury, nephrotic syndrome, dehydration, malignancy, or hypercoagulable state is provided
Segmental wedge-shaped lesions are less typical than in arterial renal infarction

data.description: Renal cell carcinoma is a malignant epithelial tumor of the kidney that may present as a solid renal mass with variable vascularity, hemorrhage, necrosis, or invasion of renal vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Focal renal parenchymal abnormality on ultrasound and MRI
Heterogeneous appearance of a renal lesion
Possible associated vascular finding near the renal hilum
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete expansile enhancing solid mass is clearly described
Wedge-shaped multifocal or segmental abnormalities are less typical for renal cell carcinoma
No hematuria, unexplained weight loss, palpable mass, or metastatic findings are provided

data.description: A distinct subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma that often occurs in younger patients without cirrhosis and commonly appears as a large hepatic mass with a central fibrous scar, sometimes containing calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Large heterogeneous mass in the liver
Central scar-like area within the hepatic mass
Possible calcification within the central scar
Mass effect on adjacent upper-abdominal structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, age, liver-function abnormalities, or cirrhosis history are provided

data.description: A benign hyperplastic liver lesion, often incidentally found, characterized by a central stellate fibrous scar and typically occurring in otherwise normal liver tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Solitary liver mass
Central scar-like appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Very large size is less typical for focal nodular hyperplasia
Possible central calcification is uncommon
Markedly heterogeneous appearance is less typical than the usually homogeneous appearance of focal nodular hyperplasia
No clinical symptoms, age, or contrast-enhancement pattern are provided

data.description: A benign hepatocellular tumor that may become large and heterogeneous because of hemorrhage, necrosis, or fat content; it is often associated with estrogen exposure, anabolic steroids, obesity, or metabolic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Large solitary hepatic mass
Heterogeneous internal appearance
Potential mass effect from a large lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: A central fibrous scar is not typical of hepatic adenoma
Central calcification is not typical
No history of hormonal exposure, anabolic steroid use, obesity, or metabolic risk factors is provided

data.description: A primary malignant tumor of hepatocytes, most commonly arising in a cirrhotic liver or in patients with chronic hepatitis B or C infection; large tumors can become heterogeneous from necrosis or hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Large heterogeneous liver mass
Possible internal necrosis or scar-like central low-density region
Mass effect on adjacent structures
symptoms_not_in_common: A distinct central stellate scar with possible calcification is more characteristic of fibrolamellar carcinoma than conventional hepatocellular carcinoma
No cirrhosis, chronic viral hepatitis, elevated alpha-fetoprotein level, or liver dysfunction is provided

data.diagnosis: Dominant optic atrophy (OPA1-related hereditary optic neuropathy)
data.description: A hereditary mitochondrial optic neuropathy causing slowly progressive, usually bilateral and symmetric optic nerve dysfunction with temporal optic disc pallor and retinal nerve fiber layer loss.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic disc pallor/optic atrophy appearance
Bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning on OCT
Relatively symmetric involvement of both eyes
No obvious intracranial mass or demyelinating lesion on the provided MRI images
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported family history of similar visual loss
No reported gradual central visual loss, dyschromatopsia, or cecocentral scotomas

data.description: A maternally inherited mitochondrial optic neuropathy that typically causes painless central visual loss, often sequentially involving both eyes, with peripapillary vascular tortuosity early and later optic atrophy.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic nerve atrophy/pallor
Marked retinal vessel tortuosity around the optic discs
Bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
No structural brain lesion apparent on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported acute or subacute painless central visual loss
No reported sequential onset between eyes
No reported color vision loss or central/cecocentral visual field defect
Fundus findings appear atrophic rather than showing acute disc swelling

data.diagnosis: Bilateral optic neuritis related to multiple sclerosis or other inflammatory demyelinating disease
data.description: Inflammation and demyelination of the optic nerves can cause visual loss, impaired color vision, pain with eye movement, and eventual optic atrophy with retinal nerve fiber layer thinning.
symptoms_in_common: Optic nerve atrophy can occur after prior optic neuritis
Reduced retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in both eyes
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported painful eye movements
No reported acute visual loss episodes
No reported neurologic symptoms suggestive of demyelination
Provided brain and spinal MRI images do not show typical obvious demyelinating plaques

data.diagnosis: Normal-tension glaucoma or advanced primary open-angle glaucoma
data.description: A chronic optic neuropathy characterized by progressive retinal ganglion-cell and retinal nerve fiber loss, optic disc cupping, and corresponding visual field defects; it can occur even with normal intraocular pressure.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
Superior and inferior sectoral OCT abnormalities
Possible chronic bilateral optic neuropathy appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: The optic discs appear more pale than typically glaucomatous
No reported optic disc cupping or increased cup-to-disc ratio
No reported intraocular pressure elevation
No reported glaucomatous visual field loss

data.diagnosis: Nutritional, toxic, or medication-related optic neuropathy
data.description: Bilateral toxic or nutritional optic neuropathy causes symmetric retinal ganglion-cell injury and optic atrophy, commonly with painless progressive central visual loss and color vision impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral and relatively symmetric optic atrophy
Bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning
No focal compressive brain lesion apparent on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported alcohol, tobacco, toxin, or medication exposure
No reported malnutrition or vitamin deficiency
No reported central visual loss, dyschromatopsia, or cecocentral scotoma

An autosomal-recessive disorder caused by ATP7B dysfunction, resulting in impaired copper excretion, copper accumulation in the liver, brain, and cornea, and hepatic and neurologic disease.

data.description: A group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by excessive iron deposition in the basal ganglia, often causing dystonia, parkinsonism, cognitive decline, and characteristic MRI changes.
symptoms_in_common: Evidence of deep basal ganglia metal deposition on MRI
Basal ganglia degeneration and bilateral signal abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Pathogenic homozygous ATP7B variant strongly indicating a copper-metabolism disorder
Corneal Kayser-Fleischer-ring-like finding
Hepatic biopsy findings suggesting liver involvement
T1 hyperintensity described as heavy-metal deposition, whereas iron accumulation more commonly causes T2/SWI hypointensity

data.diagnosis: Manganese deposition due to chronic liver disease or portosystemic shunting
data.description: Manganese accumulation in the basal ganglia can occur in advanced chronic liver disease or portosystemic shunting and typically produces bilateral T1 hyperintensity in the globus pallidus, sometimes with parkinsonian neurologic manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral basal ganglia T1 hyperintensity compatible with metal deposition
Evidence of hepatic involvement on liver histology
Basal ganglia abnormalities that may occur in chronic liver dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Homozygous pathogenic ATP7B c.2333G>T (p.Arg778Leu) mutation
Kayser-Fleischer-ring-like corneal finding, which is characteristic of copper deposition
Basal ganglia T2, DWI, and FLAIR abnormalities suggesting degenerative injury beyond typical isolated manganese deposition

data.description: A chronic, intensely itchy autoimmune blistering skin disease associated with gluten sensitivity/celiac disease, typically causing grouped papules, vesicles, and excoriations on extensor surfaces.
symptoms_in_common: Red papules and plaques on the extensor surfaces of the elbows
Bilateral/symmetric elbow involvement
Excoriated or inflamed-appearing lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly visible grouped vesicles or small blisters
No gastrointestinal symptoms or gluten-related history provided

data.description: A chronic inflammatory skin disorder producing well-demarcated erythematous plaques with scale, commonly affecting the elbows and other extensor surfaces.
symptoms_in_common: Red inflammatory plaques over the elbows
Extensor-surface distribution
Possible bilateral involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No obvious thick silvery scale is visible
Lesions appear more papular/excoriated than classic sharply demarcated plaques
No scalp, nail, or other typical psoriasis findings are provided

data.description: A pruritic inflammatory dermatitis that can cause erythematous papules, patches, excoriations, and chronic thickened skin; it may involve the elbows, especially in adults.
symptoms_in_common: Red inflamed patches and papules around the elbows
Excoriated-looking skin consistent with scratching
Possible bilateral involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: The extensor elbow distribution is less typical than flexural involvement in adults
No dry skin, lichenification, personal atopy, asthma, or allergic rhinitis history is provided

data.description: An inflammatory skin reaction caused by direct contact with an allergen or irritant, producing localized redness, itching, papules, vesicles, or plaques.
symptoms_in_common: Localized erythema and papular plaques on the elbows
Possible irritation or scratching changes
Lesions could correspond to contact or pressure areas
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear exposure to a new topical product, clothing material, occupational chemical, or adhesive is provided
The bilateral distribution may be less consistent with a single localized contact exposure
No sharply outlined geometric pattern is visible

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH, Forestier disease)
data.description: A noninflammatory enthesopathic disorder characterized by bulky, flowing ossification of ligaments and entheses, commonly along the anterior longitudinal ligament of the spine.
symptoms_in_common: Bulky flowing anterior ossification/osteophyte formation across multiple contiguous cervical vertebrae on CT
Relative preservation of several intervertebral disc spaces
Prominent anterior cervical bony overgrowth that can narrow or displace the pharyngeal-esophageal region
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as dysphagia, neck stiffness, aspiration, or airway difficulty were provided

data.diagnosis: Cervical spondylosis with large anterior osteophytes
data.description: Age-related degenerative disease of the cervical spine involving disc degeneration, vertebral endplate changes, and osteophyte formation.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior cervical vertebral osteophytes
Degenerative-appearing changes in the cervical spine
Possible reduction of disc height at lower cervical levels
symptoms_not_in_common: The extensive flowing ossification over multiple vertebrae is more suggestive of DISH than routine focal cervical spondylosis
No reported neck pain, radicular arm pain, numbness, weakness, or myelopathic symptoms

data.description: A chronic inflammatory spondyloarthritis that can cause spinal ankylosis through formation of thin marginal syndesmophytes and fusion of spinal joints.
symptoms_in_common: Multilevel bridging ossification involving the cervical spine
symptoms_not_in_common: Ossification appears bulky and non-marginal rather than thin marginal syndesmophytes
No reported inflammatory back pain, prolonged morning stiffness, sacroiliac disease, uveitis, or peripheral arthritis
No reported facet-joint fusion or classic bamboo-spine appearance

data.description: Hypoglycemia caused by insulin secretagogue medications, which stimulate pancreatic beta cells to release endogenous insulin.
symptoms_in_common: Documented hypoglycemia (glucose 2.4 mmol/L)
Elevated insulin level
Elevated C-peptide level, consistent with endogenous insulin production
Low beta-hydroxybutyrate, as insulin suppresses ketone production
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of diabetes treatment, sulfonylurea use, meglitinide use, or accidental medication ingestion was provided
No typical hypoglycemia symptoms such as sweating, tremor, palpitations, confusion, or seizures were described

data.description: A rare autoimmune condition in which insulin autoantibodies bind and later release insulin, producing spontaneous episodes of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia without exogenous insulin exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Documented hypoglycemia
Markedly elevated insulin concentration during hypoglycemia
C-peptide is not suppressed, supporting endogenous insulin secretion
Low beta-hydroxybutyrate consistent with insulin-mediated hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No information was provided about insulin autoantibodies
No history of exposure to triggering medications or supplements, such as alpha-lipoic acid or sulfhydryl-containing drugs, was provided
Insulin levels in insulin autoimmune syndrome are often extremely high, sometimes substantially higher than the reported level

data.description: Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction causing excessive endogenous insulin secretion, often associated with postprandial hypoglycemia and sometimes occurring after bariatric surgery.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia with elevated endogenous insulin
Elevated C-peptide level
Low beta-hydroxybutyrate during hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No information was provided about postprandial timing of hypoglycemia
No history of bariatric surgery was provided
No recurrent symptomatic episodes such as dizziness, confusion, sweating, or tremor were described

data.description: A condition in which hypermobile false ribs, usually the 8th to 10th ribs, move excessively at their cartilaginous attachments and may slip beneath an adjacent rib, irritating intercostal nerves.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearance involving the lower false ribs (7th-9th ribs)
Apparent abnormal relationship or overlap/mobility of the 8th rib relative to adjacent ribs
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as intermittent lower chest pain, upper abdominal pain, clicking, or pain triggered by movement are provided

data.diagnosis: Rib fracture with displacement or healing callus
data.description: A break in a rib that may produce cortical irregularity, step-off deformity, displacement, or callus formation during healing.
symptoms_in_common: Possible irregular contour or altered alignment of the 8th rib on ultrasound
Localized abnormality affecting a rib
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported traumatic event
No reported focal chest-wall tenderness
No reported pain with breathing, coughing, or movement
No definite fracture line is described

data.description: A developmental variation in rib shape, spacing, fusion, or costochondral anatomy that can alter the appearance and relationship of adjacent ribs.
symptoms_in_common: Unusual anatomical relationship among the 7th, 8th, and 9th ribs on ultrasound
Possible structural contour variation of the 8th rib
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of a longstanding chest-wall deformity is provided
No congenital history is provided
No associated respiratory or musculoskeletal symptoms are provided

data.description: A condition characterized by multiple gas-filled cysts within the bowel wall, often affecting the colon. It may be benign/idiopathic or secondary to bowel, pulmonary, infectious, ischemic, or medication-related conditions.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple clustered, grape-like submucosal cystic lesions in the colon on barium examination
Smooth polypoid/submucosal bulges seen at colonoscopy
Endoscopic ultrasound appearance of intramural gas-containing cysts with acoustic shadowing
Histology showing empty cystic spaces in the bowel wall with surrounding inflammatory/foreign-body giant-cell reaction

data.description: A benign malformation of lymphatic vessels that can produce multiple submucosal cystic lesions in the gastrointestinal tract, usually containing clear lymphatic fluid rather than gas.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple smooth submucosal polypoid lesions on colonoscopy
Cystic-appearing lesions within the colonic wall
symptoms_not_in_common: Barium appearance suggesting gas-filled grape-like cysts
Endoscopic ultrasound acoustic shadowing typical of intramural gas
Histologic empty spaces with foreign-body giant-cell reaction to gas cysts

data.diagnosis: Colonic pneumatosis due to bowel ischemia
data.description: Intramural bowel gas caused by intestinal ischemia or infarction, often associated with severe abdominal pain and potentially life-threatening bowel injury. Imaging may show linear or cystic gas in the bowel wall.
symptoms_in_common: Intramural gas-containing cystic spaces in the colon
Gas-related acoustic shadowing on endoscopic ultrasound
Bowel-wall cystic/air lucencies on contrast radiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-circumscribed, chronic-appearing grape-like submucosal cyst clusters
Benign-appearing smooth mucosa over multiple cysts
No provided evidence of acute severe pain, systemic toxicity, bowel-wall necrosis, or portal venous gas

data.description: A group of disorders characterized by numerous colorectal polyps, including adenomatous, hamartomatous, or serrated polyps; these lesions arise from mucosa rather than being gas-filled intramural cysts.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple polypoid elevations visible during colonoscopy
Multiple filling-defect-like abnormalities on contrast colon imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Submucosal translucent cystic appearance rather than mucosal polyps
Intramural gas with posterior acoustic shadowing on endoscopic ultrasound
Histology showing gas cyst spaces and giant-cell reaction rather than epithelial polyp proliferation

data.description: Hallazgos de laboratorio: leucocitos 7.700/μL con eosinofilia marcada (53,5%; eosinófilos 4.120/μL), anemia (glóbulos rojos 3,66 millones/μL, Hgb 8,6 g/dL) y CRP elevada 2,66 mg/dL. La bioquímica mostró función renal normal (BUN 12,0 mg/dL, creatinina 0,90 mg/dL) e hipoalminemia leve (albúmina 3,5 g/dL). AST 15 U/L, ALT 11 U/L, LDH 243 U/L, ALP 176 U/L, colesterol total 156 mg/dL, triglicéridos 86 mg/dL y receptor soluble de IL-2 495 U/mL. Las pruebas autoinmunes e infecciosas fueron negativas: ANA, anticuerpo Jo-1, RF, PR-ANCA, MPO-ANCA, HBsAg, HBsAb, anticuerpo contra el VHC y anticuerpo contra el VIH. La gasometría arterial mostró pH 7,549, pCO2 27,1 mmHg, pO2 68,2 mmHg y HCO3 23,1 mmol/L.

data.diagnosis: Leucemia eosinofílica crónica, no especificada de otra manera (CEL-NOS)
data.description: Una neoplasia mieloide clonal caracterizada por hipereosinofilia persistente, maduración anormal de eosinófilos, citopenias y/o displasia, tras la exclusión de causas reactivas y específicas asociadas al gen de fusión de eosinofilia.
symptoms_in_common: Eosinofilia absoluta marcada (4.120/μL; 53,5%)
Formas eosinófilas inmaduras circulantes, incluyendo mieloicitos eosinofílicos, metamieloicitos y bandas
Anemia (hemoglobina 8,6 g/dL)
Características displásicas en la película sanguínea, incluyendo neutrófilos hipersegmentados irregulares y células similares a megaloblastos
Anomalía citogenética que afecta los cromosomas 1 y 7, que sostiene un trastorno hematológico clonal
Elevación leve de marcadores inflamatorios (PCR 2,66 mg/dL)
symptoms_not_in_common: No hay leucocitosis; el recuento total de leucocitos es normal
No se documentan esplenomegalia, hepatomegalia, fiebre, pérdida de peso, erupción cutánea, afectación cardíaca ni complicaciones trombóticas
No se ha reportado un aumento en las explosiones

data.diagnosis: síndrome mielodisplásico con eosinofilia y der(1; 7)(q10; p10) anomalía
data.description: Una neoplasia mieloide con producción ineficaz de células sanguíneas y displasia. Cromossoma derivado 1; 7 anomalías recurrentes en síndromes mielodisplásicos y pueden estar asociadas con anemia, displasia multilineal y eosinofilia.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia significativa
Anomalías eritroides similares a megaloblastos en la frotiga periférica
Neutrófilos irregulares hipersegmentados que sugieren disgranulopoiesis
Maduración anormal de eosinófilos con bandas eosinofílicas y precursores eosinofílicos inmaduros
Anomalía del cromosoma 1 y cromosoma 7 de apariencia clonal
Recuento total de leucocitos normal o solo ligeramente alterado
symptoms_not_in_common: La eosinofilia marcada es poco común en la mayoría de los síndromes mielodisplásicos
No se proporciona recuento de plaquetas ni trombocitopenia
No se proporciona porcentaje de blastos de médula ósea para clasificar el subtipo de MDS
No se ha reportado historial de dependencia a transfusiones ni citopenia crónica

data.description: Un grupo de solapamiento de trastornos mieloides clonales que muestran tanto hematopoyesis displásica como características proliferativas como eosinofilia o aumento de precursores mieloides. Se necesitan pruebas moleculares para distinguir esto de CEL-NOS y neoplasias eosinofílicas asociadas a fusión.
symptoms_in_common: Hipereosinofilia persistente
Precursores granulocíticos y eosinofílicos inmaduros en la sangre periférica
Anemia
Morfología displástica de neutrófilos y eritroides
Anomalía citogenética clonal
Elevación leve de marcadores inflamatorios
symptoms_not_in_common: No hay leucocitosis ni trombocitosis claras, que son características proliferativas frecuentes
No hay esplenomegalia documentada
No se ha reportado monocitosis
No se proporcionan hallazgos de médula ósea

data.diagnosis: Neoplasia mieloide/linfoide con eosinofilia y reordenamiento génico de tirosina-quinasa (por ejemplo, reordenamiento de PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 o PCM1-JAK2)
data.description: Un grupo de neoplasias hematológicas clonales impulsadas por reordenamientos que involucran genes tirosina-quinasa. Comúnmente causan eosinofilia marcada y pueden producir anemia, hallazgos displásicos de médula y síntomas constitucionales o de afectación orgánica.
symptoms_in_common: Eosinofilia absoluta marcada
Precursores eosinófilos inmaduros en la sangre periférica
Anemia
Posible anomalía cromosómica clonal
Pruebas autoinmunes y víricas infecciosas comunes negativas, lo que hace menos probable la eosinofilia reactiva
symptoms_not_in_common: La anomalía cromosómica representada involucra los cromosomas 1 y 7 en lugar de una reorganización documentada de PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 o JAK2
No se ha reportado esplenomegalia ni hepatomegalia
No se ha reportado daño cardíaco, pulmonar, gastrointestinal, cutáneo u órgano neurológico mediado por eosinófilos
No se proporciona ningún resultado de pruebas de fusión molecular

data.diagnosis: Rosai-Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy)
data.description: A rare non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder characterized by accumulation of S100-positive histiocytes, often showing emperipolesis on histology. It can cause painless lymphadenopathy and extranodal disease involving the gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, skin, and other organs.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal lymphadenopathy involving thoracic and abdominal regions
Abdominal soft-tissue masses or nodal conglomerates
Bowel wall involvement with possible intestinal narrowing or obstruction
Renal/perirenal infiltrative lesions
Histology showing large histiocyte-like cells in an inflammatory background
Immunohistochemical pattern consistent with histiocytic disease, including S100-positive cells
symptoms_not_in_common: No classic report of massive painless cervical lymphadenopathy
No reported fever, night sweats, weight loss, or markedly elevated inflammatory markers
No reported cutaneous lesions

data.description: A clonal histiocytic neoplasm involving Langerhans cells, which may affect bone, skin, lungs, lymph nodes, liver, spleen, and occasionally the gastrointestinal tract. Lesions typically express CD1a and langerin (CD207).
symptoms_in_common: Possible multisystem infiltrative disease
Lymph node enlargement
Abdominal organ or gastrointestinal involvement can occur
Histiocytic-appearing inflammatory lesion on tissue sampling
symptoms_not_in_common: No described lytic bone lesions
No skull, jaw, rib, or long-bone lesions
No diabetes insipidus or pituitary involvement
No reported skin rash or seborrheic dermatitis-like lesions
The described histologic pattern is more suggestive of Rosai-Dorfman disease than typical Langerhans cells

data.description: A malignant proliferation of lymphoid cells that can present with generalized lymphadenopathy, abdominal masses, bowel infiltration, renal lesions, and bowel obstruction, particularly in pediatric or young patients.
symptoms_in_common: Mediastinal and abdominal lymphadenopathy
Abdominal nodal masses
Possible bowel infiltration and obstructive bowel gas pattern
Possible renal involvement
Multifocal fluorodeoxyglucose-avid disease on metabolic imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology appears dominated by histiocytes and inflammatory cells rather than a monomorphic malignant lymphoid population
No reported B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss

data.description: Purpura fulminans is a rapidly progressive thrombotic skin and coagulation disorder, usually caused by severe sepsis with DIC. It produces widespread purpura, skin necrosis, thrombocytopenia, and multiorgan dysfunction.

Profound thrombocytopenia
Prolonged coagulation studies early in the illness
Schistocytes and falling hemoglobin compatible with DIC-associated hemolysis
Severe metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate
Acute renal dysfunction
Marked liver enzyme elevation
Leukocyte abnormalities during severe infection
Hypoalbuminemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Macrocytosis
Tear-drop cells
Dohle bodies and toxic granulation are evidence of the underlying bacterial infection rather than purpura fulminans itself

data.diagnosis: Septic shock with disseminated intravascular coagulation
data.description: Septic shock is life-threatening infection-associated circulatory and metabolic failure. Severe cases can trigger DIC, causing thrombocytopenia, abnormal coagulation tests, microvascular thrombosis, bleeding, hemolysis, and multiorgan injury.
symptoms_in_common: Critical illness with severe lactic acidosis
Initial leukopenia followed by leukocytosis
Dohle bodies and toxic neutrophil granulation
Severe thrombocytopenia
Prolonged aPTT and mildly prolonged PT/INR
Schistocytes with worsening anemia
Purpura/ecchymoses consistent with coagulopathy
Acute kidney injury
Severe acute transaminitis consistent with hypoperfusion/shock liver
Hyponatremia
Hypocalcemia and hypoalbuminemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Macrocytosis
Tear-drop cells
Persistently normalizing PT/INR despite ongoing severe thrombocytopenia is less typical of untreated progressive DIC

data.description: TTP is a thrombotic microangiopathy, usually caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, characterized by thrombocytopenia and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with variable kidney, neurologic, and fever manifestations. Coagulation studies are generally normal.

Progressive anemia
Schistocytes on peripheral smear
Acute kidney injury
Purpuric skin findings

Severe lactic acidosis from septic shock
Very high acute AST/ALT consistent with shock liver

Macrocytosis and tear-drop cells are not typical TTP findings

data.diagnosis: Acute right middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke
data.description: An acute infarction caused by interruption of blood flow to the right cerebral hemisphere, commonly from occlusion of the internal carotid artery or middle cerebral artery.

MR angiography shows markedly reduced or absent flow in the right internal carotid/right anterior circulation
Imaging pattern is compatible with a large-vessel ischemic stroke
symptoms_not_in_common: Intracardiac echogenic mass/thrombus seen on echocardiography is not a direct brain-stroke symptom, although it may be the embolic source

data.diagnosis: Cardioembolic ischemic stroke due to left ventricular thrombus
data.description: A cerebral infarction caused by embolization of a thrombus formed within the left ventricle, often in the setting of reduced ventricular wall motion, prior myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy, or ventricular aneurysm.

Large-vessel occlusion involving the right anterior cerebral circulation
Echocardiographic evidence of a left-sided intracardiac mass compatible with thrombus
Pattern supports embolic occlusion of an intracranial artery

data.diagnosis: Left atrial myxoma with cerebral embolic stroke
data.description: A left atrial myxoma is a benign cardiac tumor that can shed tumor fragments or surface thrombus, causing embolic ischemic stroke and occlusion of cerebral arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Left-sided intracardiac mass on echocardiography
Acute ischemic infarction with an embolic-appearing large-vessel occlusion

data.diagnosis: Right internal carotid artery occlusion with artery-to-artery embolic stroke
data.description: Occlusion of the internal carotid artery, often from atherosclerotic thrombosis, embolism, or less commonly dissection, can produce a large ipsilateral middle cerebral artery territory infarct.

Right hemispheric infarct is in the expected vascular territory downstream from carotid occlusion

symptoms_not_in_common: Intracardiac mass/thrombus suggests a potential cardiac embolic source rather than isolated carotid atherosclerotic disease

data.description: Los hallazgos de laboratorio al ingresar mostraron enzimas hepáticas y bilirrubina elevadas, con ALT 327 U/L, AST 104 U/L, fosfatasa alcalina 172 U/L, bilirrubina total 5,8 mg/dL y CA 19-9 73 U/mL. La glucosa fue de 162 mg/dL. El hemograma, los electrolitos, la función renal y las plaquetas estuvieron dentro de los límites normales. Las analíticas repetidas en el segundo hospital mostraron hiperbilirrubinemia persistente y transaminita, con AST 267 U/L, ALT 85 U/L, fosfatasa alcalina 150 U/L, bilirrubina total 6,7 mg/dL y CA 19-9 79 U/mL.
Un adenocarcinoma maligno que surge en el conducto biliar extrahepático, que a menudo causa obstrucción biliar progresiva y ictericia.

Fosfatasa alcalina elevada compatible con colestasis
ALT y AST elevados
CA ligeramente elevada 19-9
Apariencia por imagen de la obstrucción biliar con dilatación del sistema biliar y vesícula biliar distendida
Imágenes de citología/histología compatibles con adenocarcinoma con reacción estromal desmotásica
symptoms_not_in_common: El hemograma y las plaquetas normales no son inusuales, pero no apoyan específicamente el diagnóstico
La hiperglucemia es inespecífica

data.diagnosis: Adenocarcinoma pancreático ductal de la cabeza pancreática
data.description: Un cáncer de páncreas que surge en la cabeza del páncreas y puede obstruir el conducto biliar común distal, produciendo ictericia obstructiva indolora y un aumento de CA 19-9.
symptoms_in_common: Hiperbilirrubinemia debido a una posible obstrucción distal del conducto biliar
Fosfatasa alcalina elevada y transaminasas
Elevación suave CA 19-9
Vesícula biliar distendida y dilatación ductal biliar en la imagen
Glucosa elevada, que puede ocurrir con cáncer de páncreas o diabetes

No se han reportado pérdidas de peso, dolor abdominal ni anorexia

data.diagnosis: Carcinoma de vesícula biliar con extensión biliar
data.description: Una malignidad de la vesícula biliar, generalmente adenocarcinoma, que puede invadir el hígado o los conductos biliares extrahepáticos y causar ictericia obstructiva.
symptoms_in_common: La ictericia reflejada por un aumento de bilirrubina
Anomalías colestáticas en enzimas hepáticas
Puede producirse un CA elevado entre 19 y 9
Se pueden observar citologías e histologías tipo adenocarcinoma
Posible obstrucción biliar en la imagen

symptoms_in_common: Bilirrubina elevada
Fosfatasa alcalina elevada
ALT y AST elevados
Una elevación leve de CA 19-9 puede darse en colestasis benigna
La dilatación ductal biliar y la distensión de la vesícula biliar pueden producirse con obstrucción
symptoms_not_in_common: Las imágenes de citología/histología sugieren células malignas formadoras de glándulas en lugar de un proceso obstructivo puramente benigno
La obstrucción persistente con una lesión masiva sospechosa es menos común en la enfermedad de cálculos no complicada
No se han reportado cólicos biliares, fiebre, leucocitosis ni pancreatitis

data.description: Inflammation of the appendix, usually caused by obstruction of the appendiceal lumen. MRI may show a dilated, thick-walled appendix with surrounding inflammatory change.

Possible focal bowel-wall thickening on MRI

Possible bowel-wall thickening

data.description: A fracture involving the upper surface of the tibia at the knee joint, often caused by axial loading or valgus force and sometimes associated with depression of the lateral joint surface.

Possible alteration of the lateral tibiofemoral joint contour

data.description: A follicular disorder in which multiple retained vellus hairs and keratin accumulate within dilated hair follicles, producing dark, rough, comedo-like follicular papules.

Mild perifollicular inflammatory-cell infiltrate

Follicular keratin plugging
Possible mild surrounding redness

Multiple retained hair shafts within individual follicles

data.description: Inflammation of hair follicles, often caused by bacterial, fungal, mechanical, or occlusive factors, which usually presents with follicular red papules or pustules.

data.description: A thrombotic disorder of small dermal blood vessels causing recurrent painful ulcers around the ankles and lower legs, often healing with white stellate scars called atrophie blanche.

Crusted healing lesion/scarring near the ankle

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis affecting small- and medium-sized arteries in the skin, commonly producing tender nodules, livedo reticularis, purpura, and painful leg ulcers.

Vascular injury seen on histology

data.description: An inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis that causes rapidly progressive painful ulcers, typically with a purulent base and undermined violaceous borders; it may be associated with inflammatory bowel disease, arthritis, or blood disorders.

Crusted or necrotic ulcer base

Chronic-appearing lower-leg skin changes

data.description: A rare malignant vascular tumor composed of epithelioid endothelial cells, often arranged in cords or nests within a myxohyaline stroma. data.description: An aggressive malignant endothelial tumor with markedly atypical epithelioid cells and variable vasoformative spaces. It commonly expresses vascular markers including CD31, ERG, FLI1, and sometimes CD34.

data.description: A benign or locally aggressive vascular neoplasm composed of plump epithelioid endothelial cells lining well-formed vessels, often accompanied by inflammation, especially eosinophils.

data.description: A metastatic epithelial malignancy can form nests or cords of atypical epithelioid cells and may mimic a vascular tumor, particularly when the primary site is unknown. symptoms_in_common: Hallazgos compatibles con diabetes insípida central: hipernatremia severa, hiperosmolalidad y orina insuficientemente concentrada
Múltiples deficiencias hormonales de la hipófisis anterior, incluyendo hipotiroidismo central, insuficiencia suprarrenal secundaria, hipogonadismo hipogonadotrópico y IGF-1 bajo
Hiperprolactinemia compatible con disfunción del tallo hipofisario
Lesión hipotálamo-hipofisaria del pedúnculo/suprasellar en la imagen
symptoms_not_in_common: No se han reportado lesiones óseas, erupciones cutáneas, enfermedades pulmonares, linfadenopatía u otras manifestaciones sistémicas de histiocitosis de células de Langerhans
Las lesiones de realce intracraneal pineales o multifocales son menos típicas que el germinoma intracraneal

data.diagnosis: Neurosarcoidosis que afecta al hipotálamo y al tallo hipofisario
data.description: La neurosarcoidosis es una inflamación granulomatosa del sistema nervioso que puede afectar al hipotálamo, el tallo hipofisario, las meninges y los nervios craneales. Puede causar diabetes insípida, hiperprolactinemia y panhipopituitarismo.
symptoms_in_common: Hipernatremia severa e hiperosmolalidad compatibles con diabetes insípida central
Concentración de orina inapropiadamente modesta durante la hipernatremia
Hipotiroidismo central, insuficiencia suprarrenal secundaria, hipogonadismo hipogonadotrópico y IGF-1 bajo
Prolactina elevada compatible con inflamación hipotalámica o del tallo
Aumento de la lesión de la región hipotalámica-hipofisaria
symptoms_not_in_common: No se han reportado sarcoidosis pulmonares, adenopatía hilar, uveítis, lesiones cutáneas, parálisis facial u otros hallazgos sistémicos de sarcoides
El LCR es relativamente poco destacable salvo por una proteína elevada; la neurosarcoidosis suele producir anomalías inflamatorias más prominentes del LCR
Las lesiones pineales discretas o multifocales en forma de masa favorecen el germinoma con mayor fuerza

data.diagnosis: Linfoma primario del sistema nervioso central o linfoma secundario que afecta a la región hipotalámica-hipofisaria
data.description: El linfoma puede infiltrarse en el hipotálamo, el tallo hipofisario, la región pineal o las estructuras periventriculares y puede causar diabetes insípida central y disfunción de la hipófisis anterior.
symptoms_in_common: Aumento de lesiones intracraneales que afectan a las regiones hipotalámica-hipofisarias y de la línea media profunda
Hipernatremia y osmolalidad sérica elevada compatibles con diabetes insípida central
Múltiples deficiencias hormonales de la hipófisis
Prolactina elevada compatible con afectación del tallo o hipotálamo
La citología del LCR puede ser negativa a pesar del linfoma del SNC
symptoms_not_in_common: No hay síntomas constitucionales documentados, inmunosupresión, linfoma sistémico conocido ni linfadenopatía
No se encontraron células malignas en la citología del LCR
La presentación endocrina característica con lesiones combinadas pineales y supraselares es más sugestiva de germinoma

data.description: A rare congenital anomaly in which a fibromuscular membrane divides the left atrium into two chambers, potentially obstructing pulmonary venous flow and producing physiology similar to mitral stenosis.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic appearance of a membrane within the left atrium
Apparent subdivision of the left atrial cavity on echocardiography
Notched/bifid P-wave morphology in lead II, which can suggest left atrial enlargement

data.description: A congenital fibrous membrane located just above the mitral valve that obstructs left ventricular inflow and can mimic congenital mitral stenosis.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic membrane-like structure near the mitral inflow region
Potential left atrial enlargement suggested by bifid or notched P waves
symptoms_not_in_common: A membrane dividing the left atrial cavity more proximally is more characteristic of cor triatriatum than of a supramitral ring

data.description: Narrowing of the mitral valve that obstructs blood flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle, causing elevated left atrial pressure and possible left atrial enlargement.
symptoms_in_common: Possible left atrial enlargement suggested by broad or notched P waves in lead II
An echocardiographic appearance that may suggest obstruction at the mitral inflow level
symptoms_not_in_common: A distinct intra-left-atrial membrane is not typical of ordinary rheumatic or degenerative mitral stenosis
No reported symptoms such as exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations, hemoptysis, or fatigue

data.diagnosis: Infantile-onset Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II)
data.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) deficiency, leading to glycogen accumulation in cardiac, skeletal, and respiratory muscle. Classic infantile disease causes severe hypotonia, cardiomyopathy, and respiratory failure.
symptoms_in_common: Infant presentation
Chest radiograph suggestive of cardiomegaly
Laboratory image showing markedly abnormal or absent mature GAA protein/processing
Findings compatible with a lysosomal GAA deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical description of hypotonia
No documented feeding difficulty
No documented macroglossia
No documented respiratory distress or respiratory failure

data.description: A milder form of acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency that primarily affects skeletal and respiratory muscles, usually presenting in childhood or adulthood with progressive proximal weakness and diaphragmatic weakness; significant infantile cardiomyopathy is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal GAA protein findings consistent with acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Very early infant presentation
Chest radiograph suggestive of cardiomegaly
No reported progressive limb-girdle weakness
No reported chronic diaphragmatic or nocturnal respiratory weakness

data.diagnosis: Glycogen storage disease type III (Cori disease)
data.description: A glycogen debranching enzyme deficiency causing hepatomegaly, fasting hypoglycemia, hyperlipidemia, skeletal myopathy, and sometimes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Possible cardiomegaly on chest radiograph
Infancy can be an age of presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal GAA maturation is not typical
No reported hepatomegaly
No reported fasting hypoglycemia
No reported hyperlipidemia
No reported liver dysfunction

data.description: An X-linked lysosomal/autophagy-related disorder caused by LAMP2 deficiency, characterized by hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and variable intellectual disability, usually affecting males more severely.
symptoms_in_common: Possible cardiomegaly
Potential muscle and cardiac involvement in a lysosomal-related disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal acid alpha-glucosidase protein processing is not characteristic
Typical presentation is later in childhood or adolescence rather than infancy
No reported skeletal muscle weakness
No reported developmental or cognitive impairment

data.description: Los datos de laboratorio mostraron anemia progresiva durante un año, con hematocrito descendiendo del 35,6% al 30,9% y la hemoglobina de 12,0 a 10,6 g/dL, con microcitosis desarrollándose (MCV 81,5 a 75 fL). Los marcadores inflamatorios estaban elevados: VS 41–66 mm/h y PCR 3,0–8,3 mg/dL. El recuento de glóbulos blancos estaba elevado antes (12.000–14.600/mm³) pero 7.800/mm³ al ingresar. Las plaquetas estaban normales a altas normales (352.000–433.000/mm³). Al ingresar, la ferritina estaba elevada en 470 ng/mL, LDH 517 U/L, reticulocitos 3,0% y tiempo de protrombina 14,4 seg/INR 1,2. Los anticuerpos contra Borrelia burgdorferi fueron negativos.

data.diagnosis: Linfoma de Burkitt con afectación de la médula ósea
data.description: Un linfoma no Hodgkin maduro de células B altamente agresivo, generalmente caracterizado por una rápida proliferación, LDH alta, células CD19/CD10 positivas, enfermedad extranodal y posible afectación de la médula.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia progresiva
LDH elevada
Marcadores inflamatorios elevados, incluyendo VS y PCR
Leucocitosis previa
Población de médula ósea con marcadores de células B incluyendo CD19 y CD10
Lesiones hipermetabólicas en PET/TC compatibles con afectación linfomática
symptoms_not_in_common: Progresión lenta de la anemia durante aproximadamente un año en lugar de una presentación progresiva rápida
Anemia microcítica
Solo LDH moderadamente elevada en lugar de la LDH frecuentemente elevada que se observa en el linfoma de Burkitt
Recuento de plaquetas normal a solo ligeramente elevado

data.diagnosis: Linfoma difuso de células B grandes, tipo de células B en el centro germinal
data.description: El linfoma no Hodgkin agresivo más común; está compuesto por grandes células B maduras y puede afectar ganglios linfáticos, médula ósea, tejidos extranodales, hígado, bazo y tejidos blandos. Los tumores tipo centro germinal pueden expresar CD10 y CD19.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia progresiva
LDH elevada
VS y PCR elevadas
Leucocitosis previa
Inmunofenotipo de células B con positividad CD19
Expresión CD10 compatible con la diferenciación del centro germinal
Lesiones multifocales detectadas por TEP y TC que sugieren linfoma sistémico
symptoms_not_in_common: La microcitosis no es una característica directa típica del linfoma difuso de células B grandes
La elevación de la ferritina es inespecífica y puede reflejar inflamación en lugar de linfoma solo
Recuento normal de plaquetas a pesar de la aparente implicación sistémica

data.diagnosis: Linfoma de células B de alto grado con reordenaciones de MYC y BCL2 y/o BCL6
data.description: Un linfoma agresivo de células B maduras, anteriormente conocido como linfoma de doble impacto o triple impacto, con características clínicas y morfológicas intermedias entre el linfoma difuso de células B grandes y el linfoma de Burkitt. Comúnmente se presenta con LDH elevado, enfermedad extranodal y afectación de la médula ósea.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia con empeoramiento del hematocrito y la hemoglobina
LDH elevada
Elevación de marcadores inflamatorios
Historia de la leucocitosis
Población de células B positivas para CD19 y CD10 positivas
Hallazgos de imagen preocupantes para linfoma extranodal diseminado
symptoms_not_in_common: El curso relativamente prolongado de anemia de un año puede ser menos típico de un linfoma de alto grado sin tratar
La anemia microcítica no es característica
La LDH está elevada pero no claramente extrema
Las plaquetas permanecen normales o ligeramente elevadas en lugar de reducirse por una enfermedad medular extensa

data.description: Una malignidad de los linfoblastos precursores B que puede afectar a la médula ósea, la sangre, ganglios linfáticos y sitios extranodales. Comúnmente expresa CD19 y a menudo CD10, y puede causar anemia y recuentos anómalos de glóbulos blancos.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia progresiva
Historia de la leucocitosis
Infiltrado celular anormal de médula ósea
Positividad CD19
Positividad CD10
LDH elevada
symptoms_not_in_common: La anemia microcítica no es típica de la insuficiencia medular causada por leucemia linfoblástica aguda
El recuento normal de plaquetas es menos típico cuando hay una afectación significativa de la médula
El curso prolongado de anemia indolente es menos típico de la leucemia linfoblástica aguda no tratada
La ESR elevada y la CRP no son características específicas y no definen

data.description: A bacterial infection of the deeper skin and subcutaneous tissues, causing diffuse redness, warmth, swelling, and tenderness; ultrasound may show subcutaneous edema without a discrete fluid collection.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse erythema of the buttock
Apparent swelling and induration
Inflammatory changes in the subcutaneous tissue on ultrasound
No clearly defined drainable abscess on the provided ultrasound image
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, pain severity, or laboratory inflammatory markers are provided
No visible skin break, ulcer, or purulent drainage is shown

data.description: A superficial streptococcal skin infection that produces a red, warm, swollen plaque, often with relatively well-demarcated borders and sometimes systemic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent red inflammatory skin plaque over the buttock
Localized swelling
Possible superficial soft-tissue inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: The visible erythema appears relatively diffuse rather than sharply demarcated
No fever or chills are provided
No lymphangitic streaking or enlarged regional lymph nodes are described

data.description: A localized collection of pus in the skin or subcutaneous tissue, often caused by Staphylococcus aureus, producing painful redness, swelling, and sometimes fluctuance or drainage.
symptoms_in_common: Localized buttock erythema
Swelling of the affected area
Surrounding inflammatory soft-tissue changes on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear fluid-filled cavity or drainable collection is evident on the ultrasound image
No fluctuant mass, pustule, or purulent drainage is visible
The redness appears broad and diffuse rather than centered on a focal lesion

data.description: Inflammation, cellulitis, abscess formation, or foreign-body reaction after an intramuscular or subcutaneous injection, cosmetic filler, or other local procedure.
symptoms_in_common: Buttock is a common location for injections and cosmetic procedures
Localized erythema and swelling
Subcutaneous inflammatory changes on ultrasound
Possible focal abnormality in the superficial soft tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of recent injection, filler placement, trauma, or procedure is provided
No injection puncture site, drainage, or foreign material is clearly visible

data.description: A rapidly progressive, potentially life-threatening infection involving fascia and deeper soft tissues. It can initially resemble cellulitis but is usually associated with severe pain, systemic illness, rapidly spreading erythema, skin necrosis, bullae, or soft-tissue gas.
symptoms_in_common: Extensive erythema and swelling of the buttock
Soft-tissue edema on ultrasound
Possible small echogenic focus that could warrant evaluation for gas or foreign material
symptoms_not_in_common: No severe pain out of proportion, rapid deterioration, fever, hypotension, or toxic appearance is provided
No bullae, skin necrosis, crepitus, or black discoloration is visible
No definite ultrasound evidence of fascial fluid or extensive soft-tissue gas is shown

data.description: An inflammatory autoimmune muscle and skin disease characterized by distinctive photosensitive rashes and, often, proximal muscle weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Facial erythema involving the cheeks
Diffuse erythematous rash over the upper chest in a shawl or V-neck distribution
Violaceous-red papules or plaques over the dorsal hands and knuckles, compatible with Gottron papules/sign
Symmetric distribution of skin findings
symptoms_not_in_common: No visible heliotrope rash of the eyelids
No muscle weakness is described
No dysphagia, fatigue, or muscle pain is described

data.description: A multisystem autoimmune disease that can cause photosensitive facial and chest rashes, arthritis, and other organ involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral erythema across the cheeks resembling a malar distribution
Possible photosensitive rash on the upper chest
Red-purple lesions on the dorsal hands
symptoms_not_in_common: The hand lesions appear more suggestive of Gottron papules than typical lupus lesions
No oral ulcers, joint pain, fever, kidney symptoms, or systemic symptoms are described
No clear sparing of the nasolabial folds is visible

data.description: A common delayed hypersensitivity skin reaction to a medication, usually producing a symmetric widespread red maculopapular rash beginning on the trunk.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse symmetric erythematous papular eruption over the chest
Facial redness
Rash involving the extremities and hands
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent medication exposure is provided
The violaceous knuckle-centered lesions are less typical of a simple drug eruption
No fever, itching, mucosal involvement, or systemic illness is described

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis or photoallergic dermatitis
data.description: Inflammatory dermatitis triggered by contact allergens or sunlight-associated exposures, often affecting exposed areas such as the face, neck, upper chest, and hands.
symptoms_in_common: Erythema on exposed facial skin
Upper chest rash in a potentially sun-exposed distribution
Dorsal hand involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No itching, burning, scaling, vesicles, or exposure history is described
The symmetric violaceous lesions over the knuckles are not classic for contact dermatitis
The rash appears more systemic than a localized contact reaction

data.description: A disseminated stage of syphilis that may produce a generalized maculopapular or papulosquamous rash, sometimes involving the hands and other systemic findings.
symptoms_in_common: Widespread truncal rash
Papular lesions on the hands
Possible symmetric generalized skin involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No palm or sole involvement is visible
No generalized lymph node enlargement, fever, sore throat, or mucous patches are described
The facial and knuckle-predominant pattern is more suggestive of dermatomyositis than secondary syphilis

data.description: A disorder characterized by the development of numerous rapidly growing keratinizing skin tumors, usually on sun-exposed or traumatized skin. Individual lesions may resemble well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma histologically.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple papules and nodules on the upper extremities
Crateriform and ulcerated keratotic lesions
Histology showing 15 keratoacanthomas
Progressive appearance of new lesions
Isomorphic (Koebner) response after skin trauma or excision
No metastases on computed tomography
No lymphadenopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Some lesions were histologically diagnosed as verruca vulgaris
Persistent progressive course without clear spontaneous regression

data.description: A rare variant of eruptive keratoacanthoma characterized by widespread crops of small keratotic papules and nodules, often with ongoing formation of new lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Numerous eruptive keratotic papules and nodules
Histologically confirmed keratoacanthomas
Progressive course with repeated new lesions
Lesions on the extremities
Response to topical antitumor therapies including imiquimod and 5-fluorouracil
symptoms_not_in_common: Disease appears predominantly localized to the upper extremities rather than generalized over the body
No reported severe pruritus
No reported facial involvement, ectropion, or mucosal lesions
No reported hundreds to thousands of lesions

data.description: A rare inherited or sporadic condition causing recurrent crops of keratoacanthoma-like squamous tumors that typically enlarge and subsequently regress, often leaving scars.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple keratoacanthoma-like tumors
Crateriform ulcerated nodules on the limbs
Histology compatible with keratoacanthoma or well-differentiated squamous proliferation
Scarring or hypopigmented areas after lesions improve
No evidence of metastatic spread
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported family history of similar recurrent tumors
No clearly documented spontaneous regression of untreated lesions
Progressive disease despite observation rather than a predominantly self-healing course
Isomorphic response is not a classic defining feature

data.description: A malignant keratinocyte tumor that can present as rapidly enlarging hyperkeratotic or ulcerated nodules; keratoacanthoma-type lesions may be difficult to distinguish from conventional keratoacanthoma.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerated and crusted nodules
Keratotic papules and plaques on sun-exposed upper extremities
Histologic keratoacanthoma-like squamous lesions
Progressive growth of some lesions
Use of 5-fluorouracil and imiquimod for superficial keratinocytic neoplasms
symptoms_not_in_common: Very large number of lesions developing in crops is less typical for sporadic squamous cell carcinoma
No metastases or lymphadenopathy
Isomorphic response after trauma is more suggestive of eruptive keratoacanthomas
Some biopsied lesions were verruca vulgaris

data.description: Human papillomavirus-associated benign epidermal proliferations that commonly occur as rough hyperkeratotic papules on the hands and extremities and can spread through trauma-related autoinoculation.
symptoms_in_common: Papules and keratotic lesions on the hands and upper extremities
Histology showing three lesions diagnosed as verruca vulgaris
Possible isomorphic/Koebner-like spread after local trauma
Improvement with topical 5-fluorouracil or imiquimod can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple lesions were histologically confirmed as keratoacanthomas rather than warts
Large ulcerated crateriform nodules are not typical of common warts
Scarring lesions are not typical of uncomplicated verruca vulgaris
Progressive destructive tumor-like lesions are atypical for common warts

data.description: A fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) within the spinal cord, often extending over multiple spinal levels and appearing bright on T2-weighted MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Longitudinal central fluid-signal cavity within the cervical and thoracic spinal cord on MRI
MRI appearance consistent with cerebrospinal-fluid-like signal
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as dissociated loss of pain and temperature sensation, weakness, hand muscle wasting, scoliosis, or neuropathic pain were provided

data.description: Dilation of the central canal of the spinal cord by cerebrospinal fluid; it may overlap with or represent a mild form of syringomyelia.
symptoms_in_common: Central, narrow, fluid-signal cavity in the spinal cord
Cervical and thoracic spinal cord involvement on sagittal MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms of myelopathy, sensory loss, weakness, gait difficulty, or bladder dysfunction were provided
A large eccentric cord cavity would be less typical, although the shown cavity appears central

data.description: A syrinx caused by impaired cerebrospinal-fluid flow at the foramen magnum, commonly associated with Chiari type I malformation and sometimes extending through the cervical and thoracic cord.
symptoms_in_common: Long-segment cervical/thoracic syrinx-like cavity on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite cerebellar tonsillar descent or posterior fossa abnormality is demonstrated in the provided images
No occipital headache worsened by coughing or straining was provided
No balance disturbance, dysphagia, neck pain, or sensory symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: Intramedullary spinal cord tumor with associated syrinx
data.description: Tumors such as ependymoma or astrocytoma can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow or alter cord architecture, resulting in a syrinx above or below the lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Intramedullary fluid-signal abnormality that could represent a tumor-associated syrinx
symptoms_not_in_common: No visible solid intramedullary mass, cord expansion, hemorrhagic component, or contrast-enhancing lesion is shown in the provided images
No progressive weakness, sensory deficits, gait dysfunction, or bowel/bladder symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with IGH::IRS4 rearrangement
data.description: A rare subtype of precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia characterized by marrow and blood involvement by lymphoblasts and a translocation involving Xq22.3 (IRS4) and chromosome 14q32 (IGH), often written as t(X;14)(q22.3;q32).
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral blood smear with circulating immature blast-like cells
Bone marrow heavily replaced by lymphoblasts
Cytogenetic evidence of t(X;14) involving Xq22.3 and chromosome 14
FISH findings consistent with rearrangement of the IRS4 region
Additional chromosomal abnormality involving chromosomes 12 and 14
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, physical findings, blood counts, or immunophenotype results were provided

data.diagnosis: Precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma, not otherwise specified
data.description: An aggressive hematologic malignancy caused by clonal proliferation of immature B-lymphoid precursors in bone marrow, peripheral blood, and sometimes lymph nodes or other tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Numerous immature blast cells in the bone marrow
Circulating blast-like cells in peripheral blood
Marrow architecture substantially replaced by monomorphic lymphoblasts
Clonal chromosomal abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever, fatigue, pallor, bruising, bleeding, bone pain, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or recurrent infections
No flow-cytometry evidence of B-cell markers such as CD19, CD10, CD79a, TdT, or CD34 was provided

data.description: A malignancy of immature T-lymphoid cells that can produce extensive marrow and peripheral-blood blast involvement, commonly associated with T-cell receptor gene rearrangements and sometimes a mediastinal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral blood blast-like cells
Bone marrow packed with lymphoblasts
Evidence of a clonal hematologic malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: The demonstrated rearrangement involving chromosome 14q32/IGH and Xq22.3/IRS4 is more suggestive of B-lineage disease than T-lineage disease
No mediastinal mass or thymic involvement was reported
No T-cell immunophenotype, such as cytoplasmic/surface CD3, CD7, or CD2 expression, was provided

data.diagnosis: Infection-associated HLH, likely viral-triggered (including severe COVID-19-associated HLH)
data.description: A form of secondary HLH precipitated by a severe viral infection. Viral infections can cause diffuse pneumonitis and trigger excessive immune activation with very high ferritin, cytopenias, coagulopathy, and hemophagocytosis.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral diffuse lung infiltrates compatible with viral pneumonitis
Extreme ferritin elevation
Leukopenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia
Low fibrinogen
Splenomegaly
Hemophagocytosis on hematologic/pathologic images
symptoms_not_in_common: No viral PCR, antigen test, or specific infectious trigger is provided
No fever or respiratory symptom history is explicitly reported

data.description: MAS is a secondary HLH-like hyperinflammatory syndrome, most commonly associated with systemic rheumatologic disorders such as systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis or adult-onset Still disease. It causes macrophage activation, severe cytopenias, hyperferritinemia, liver/spleen enlargement, and hypofibrinogenemia.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hyperferritinemia
Pancytopenia
Hypofibrinogenemia
Splenomegaly
Hemophagocytosis
Diffuse inflammatory pulmonary abnormalities can occur in severe systemic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No known autoimmune or rheumatologic disease is described
No arthritis, evanescent rash, or characteristic quotidian fever is reported

data.description: A genetic disorder of impaired cytotoxic lymphocyte function that leads to recurrent or severe HLH, usually beginning in infancy or childhood but occasionally presenting later. It has the same core laboratory and histologic features as secondary HLH.
symptoms_in_common: Extreme hyperferritinemia
Cytopenias involving all three blood cell lines
Hypofibrinogenemia
Splenomegaly
Hemophagocytosis
Possible pulmonary involvement during severe systemic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No childhood onset, recurrent episodes, family history, or genetic testing information is provided
The imaging pattern may more strongly suggest an infectious trigger for secondary HLH

data.diagnosis: Cerebral dural arteriovenous fistula with cortical venous reflux
data.description: An abnormal connection between meningeal arteries and dural venous channels that causes retrograde drainage into cortical veins, producing venous congestion, dilated cortical veins, edema, and sometimes venous infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent serpiginous cortical vessels on imaging
Dilated cortical veins on CT angiographic imaging
Bilateral cerebral white-matter and deep gray-matter signal abnormalities consistent with venous congestion
Possible cortical/subcortical edema or venous infarction
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, such as pulsatile tinnitus, headache, seizures, focal weakness, or cognitive decline, are provided

data.diagnosis: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with cortical venous congestion
data.description: Thrombosis of a dural venous sinus can obstruct cerebral venous drainage, causing engorged collateral cortical veins, venous edema, hemorrhage, and venous infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Enlarged cortical venous structures
Parenchymal abnormalities that may represent venous edema or venous infarction
Possible bilateral involvement not conforming to a single arterial territory
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite dural venous sinus filling defect or absent sinus flow is described
No reported headache, papilledema, seizure, altered consciousness, or focal neurologic deficit

data.description: Thrombosis limited to one or more cortical cerebral veins may produce focal venous congestion, swollen or hyperintense cortical veins, and adjacent cortical-subcortical edema or hemorrhagic venous infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal prominent cortical vein indicated on imaging
Adjacent cortical and subcortical signal abnormality compatible with venous congestion
Possible venous infarct-like lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging appears to show more widespread and bilateral abnormalities than is typical for a single isolated cortical vein thrombosis
No reported headache, seizure, focal neurologic deficit, or altered mental status

data.description: A small-vessel immune-complex vasculitis characterized by IgA deposition, most often causing palpable purpura on the lower extremities and sometimes involving the gastrointestinal tract, joints, and kidneys.
symptoms_in_common: Petechial and palpable purpuric lesions predominantly on the lower legs and ankles
Hemorrhagic-appearing nasal lesion or crusting
Possible ankle and foot swelling
Skin biopsy appearance consistent with leukocytoclastic small-vessel vasculitis
Direct immunofluorescence showing vascular IgA deposition with C3 and fibrin
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, arthralgia, or renal symptoms are described

data.description: An inflammatory small-vessel vasculitis of the skin, commonly triggered by medications, infections, autoimmune disease, or other immune stimuli; it typically presents with palpable purpura on dependent areas.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric and petechial eruption on the lower legs
Lesions concentrated in dependent lower-extremity areas
Histology compatible with small-vessel vasculitis and neutrophilic vascular injury
Fibrin deposition in affected dermal vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent IgA vascular deposition is more specifically supportive of IgA vasculitis than nonspecific hypersensitivity vasculitis
Nasal hemorrhagic crusting is not a typical primary feature

data.description: A systemic ANCA-associated necrotizing vasculitis that commonly affects the upper airways, lungs, kidneys, and skin. Nasal inflammation, ulceration, crusting, and epistaxis can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Nasal crusting or hemorrhagic nasal lesion
Purpuric skin lesions that can reflect cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: IgA-dominant immune deposition is not typical; granulomatosis with polyangiitis is usually pauci-immune
No sinus disease, pulmonary symptoms, kidney symptoms, constitutional symptoms, or granulomatous inflammation are described
Lower-extremity palpable purpura with IgA deposition more strongly favors IgA vasculitis

data.description: An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis, often associated with hepatitis C infection, autoimmune disease, or lymphoproliferative disorders, causing palpable purpura and possible kidney, nerve, and joint involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Lower-extremity petechiae and palpable purpura
Immune-complex-type small-vessel vasculitis on skin biopsy
Possible complement deposition in affected vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: IgA-predominant deposition is less typical than mixed immunoglobulin and complement deposition
No neuropathy, arthralgia, weakness, renal disease, hepatitis C history, or cold sensitivity is described
Nasal crusting is not a usual manifestation

data.diagnosis: Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma with metastatic cervical lymphadenopathy
data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising in the tonsil or base of tongue/oropharynx that commonly spreads to upper cervical lymph nodes; many cases are associated with human papillomavirus (HPV).
