Enlarged left cervical lymph node with abnormal rounded hypoechoic appearance on ultrasound
FDG-avid ipsilateral cervical lymphadenopathy on PET imaging
Imaging appearance compatible with a primary head-and-neck lesion and regional nodal metastasis
symptoms_not_in_common: No sore throat, dysphagia, odynophagia, voice change, otalgia, weight loss, or tobacco/alcohol history is provided

data.description: A subtype of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, usually arising from the palatine or lingual tonsil, often presenting with a cystic or enlarged upper-neck lymph node even when the primary lesion is relatively subtle.
symptoms_in_common: Possible left tonsillar/oropharyngeal FDG-avid primary lesion
Prominent unilateral cervical nodal enlargement
Rounded, abnormal hypoechoic cervical node on ultrasound
Metabolically active cervical lymph node on PET-CT
symptoms_not_in_common: HPV status is not provided
No clinical tonsillar symptoms or neck-mass history is provided
No age, sexual history, smoking history, or pathology result is provided

data.description: Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin lymphoma can involve tonsillar lymphoid tissue and cervical lymph nodes, producing enlarged homogeneous or hypoechoic nodes and increased FDG uptake on PET imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Enlarged cervical lymph node
Hypoechoic rounded nodal appearance on ultrasound
FDG-avid lymphoid tissue in the oropharyngeal/tonsillar region
FDG-avid cervical lymphadenopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging suggests a focal oropharyngeal primary with regional nodal spread, which is more typical of squamous cell carcinoma
No generalized lymphadenopathy is described
No fever, night sweats, unexplained weight loss, pruritus, or fatigue is provided

data.diagnosis: Reactive or infectious cervical lymphadenitis with tonsillitis
data.description: Inflammation of cervical lymph nodes due to infection in the tonsils, pharynx, oral cavity, or upper respiratory tract can cause nodal enlargement and increased FDG uptake.
symptoms_in_common: Enlarged cervical lymph node
Possible increased metabolic activity in the tonsillar/oropharyngeal region
Possible unilateral tonsillar inflammatory process
symptoms_not_in_common: Rounded abnormal nodal morphology and strong focal PET uptake are concerning for malignancy rather than simple reactive lymphadenitis
No fever, sore throat, upper-respiratory symptoms, dental infection, leukocytosis, or acute tenderness is provided
A discrete suspicious oropharyngeal mass is less typical of uncomplicated infection

data.diagnosis: Nested variant urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder
data.description: A rare, deceptively bland-appearing invasive variant of urothelial carcinoma characterized by small nests of urothelial tumor cells infiltrating the lamina propria or muscularis propria. It may show chromosomal abnormalities on UroVysion fluorescence in situ hybridization testing.
symptoms_in_common: Bladder mass/lesion on gross examination
Nested infiltrative tumor-cell architecture beneath urothelium on histology
Atypical urothelial cells with enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei
Abnormal multicolor fluorescence in situ hybridization pattern consistent with chromosomal copy-number abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as hematuria, dysuria, urinary frequency, or pelvic pain were provided

data.description: The most common malignant tumor of the bladder, arising from urothelial lining cells and capable of invading the lamina propria and bladder muscle. It often has cytologic atypia, architectural disorder, and genetic abnormalities detectable by UroVysion testing.
symptoms_in_common: Grossly visible bladder tumor
Urothelial-lined surface adjacent to an underlying invasive neoplasm
Marked nuclear atypia in tumor cells
Tumor nests and cords within supporting stroma
Abnormal fluorescence in situ hybridization signals suggestive of urothelial carcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported painless gross hematuria
No reported irritative voiding symptoms
No reported urinary obstruction or flank pain

data.description: A benign urothelial neoplasm that typically forms an endophytic or inverted growth pattern composed of nests and cords of relatively bland urothelial cells. It can resemble nested urothelial carcinoma histologically, but usually lacks substantial atypia and invasive destructive growth.
symptoms_in_common: Bladder lesion
Nested or inverted growth pattern beneath the urothelial surface
Urothelial cell proliferation
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent cytologic atypia is not typical
Infiltrative-appearing nests in the stroma are not typical for a benign papilloma
Abnormal UroVysion fluorescence in situ hybridization findings are not typical
No clinical symptoms such as hematuria or dysuria were provided

data.diagnosis: Urothelial carcinoma in situ with associated invasion
data.description: A high-grade flat urothelial neoplasm in which markedly atypical cells involve the urothelial lining; it may coexist with invasive urothelial carcinoma elsewhere in the sampled lesion. Fluorescence in situ hybridization can demonstrate chromosomal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Atypical urothelial cells near the mucosal surface
High-grade nuclear features
Abnormal fluorescence in situ hybridization signals
Possible association with invasive urothelial tumor nests
symptoms_not_in_common: A predominantly nested submucosal tumor architecture is not the classic appearance of carcinoma in situ alone
A discrete gross mass is less typical for isolated carcinoma in situ
No reported hematuria, urgency, frequency, or dysuria

data.diagnosis: Bilateral developmental dysplasia of the hip with chronic subluxation/dislocation
data.description: A congenital or developmental abnormality in which shallow acetabula provide inadequate coverage of the femoral heads, leading to chronic hip subluxation or dislocation and secondary degenerative deformity.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral shallow/dysplastic acetabula
Bilateral superior-lateral displacement/subluxation of the femoral heads
Marked deformity and remodeling of both femoral heads and necks
Secondary degenerative changes of both hip joints
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, age, gait findings, or history of childhood hip instability were provided

data.description: Advanced degenerative joint disease caused by an underlying structural hip disorder, trauma, inflammatory disease, or chronic instability; it can produce joint-space loss, femoral-head deformity, sclerosis, and subluxation.
symptoms_in_common: Severe bilateral hip-joint deformity
Femoral-head flattening and irregular remodeling
Chronic hip subluxation/malalignment
Degenerative-appearing changes involving both hips
symptoms_not_in_common: The degree of acetabular dysplasia and displacement suggests an underlying structural disorder rather than primary osteoarthritis alone
No reported hip pain, stiffness, reduced range of motion, or functional limitation

data.diagnosis: Bilateral femoral head osteonecrosis (avascular necrosis) with secondary collapse
data.description: Loss of blood supply to the femoral head can cause subchondral bone death, collapse, flattening, and eventual secondary osteoarthritis. It may be bilateral, especially with corticosteroid exposure, alcohol use, sickle-cell disease, or other systemic risk factors.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral femoral-head deformity and flattening
Advanced collapse/remodeling of the proximal femora
Secondary degenerative hip-joint changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked acetabular shallowness and chronic superior-lateral subluxation are more characteristic of hip dysplasia
No reported risk factors for osteonecrosis
No reported groin pain or progressive weight-bearing pain

data.diagnosis: Chronic inflammatory arthropathy of the hips, such as rheumatoid arthritis
data.description: Inflammatory arthritis can cause progressive cartilage loss, erosions, osteopenia, femoral-head destruction, and severe functional impairment; hip involvement usually occurs in established systemic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral hip involvement
Severe joint destruction and deformity
Possible periarticular osteopenic appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Shallow dysplastic acetabula and pronounced superior-lateral displacement are not classic primary features of rheumatoid hip disease
No reported symmetric small-joint arthritis, morning stiffness, systemic inflammatory symptoms, or known autoimmune disease

data.description: A destructive arthropathy caused by impaired protective sensation, resulting in progressive joint destruction, fragmentation, subluxation, and deformity. Hip involvement is uncommon but can occur with severe neurologic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Marked joint destruction and deformity
Hip subluxation/disorganization
Bilateral involvement is possible in systemic neurologic conditions
symptoms_not_in_common: The radiographic appearance of shallow acetabula suggests developmental dysplasia more strongly
No reported sensory loss, neuropathy, diabetes, spinal cord disease, or painless destructive joint process

data.description: Displacement of the patella out of the femoral trochlear groove, usually toward the lateral side; it may be acute or recurrent and is often associated with patellar instability.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographic appearance of patellar malalignment relative to the trochlear groove
Apparent lateral displacement of the patella on the axial patellofemoral view
Possible associated patella alta, a risk factor for patellar instability

data.diagnosis: Patellofemoral instability with lateral patellar subluxation
data.description: Partial lateral displacement or maltracking of the patella during knee motion without complete persistent dislocation. It commonly occurs in patients with a shallow trochlea, patella alta, or prior dislocation.
symptoms_in_common: Patella appears laterally malpositioned on the patellofemoral view
High-riding patellar position consistent with possible patella alta
Abnormal patellofemoral alignment

data.description: An abnormally high position of the patella relative to the femur and tibia. It can be congenital or result from patellar tendon injury and predisposes to lateral patellar instability.
symptoms_in_common: High position of the patella on the lateral knee radiograph
Patellofemoral maltracking or instability appearance

data.description: A tear of the patellar tendon causing loss of the extensor mechanism and typically producing patella alta on radiographs. This is generally an acute traumatic injury.
symptoms_in_common: Patella alta on the lateral radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical history of acute trauma, anterior knee pain, swelling, or inability to actively extend the knee was provided

data.description: A neoplasm arising from pancreatic neuroendocrine cells, often appearing as a well-circumscribed, hyperenhancing pancreatic mass. Histology commonly shows relatively uniform cells in nests, trabeculae, or sheets and neuroendocrine-marker positivity.
symptoms_in_common: Pancreatic mass on contrast-enhanced CT
Relatively circumscribed solid lesion
Cellular tumor histology with monotonous-appearing cells
symptoms_not_in_common: No patient-reported clinical symptoms were provided
No hormone-excess syndrome symptoms such as hypoglycemia, diarrhea, flushing, or peptic-ulcer symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: Solid pseudopapillary neoplasm of the pancreas
data.description: A rare low-grade malignant pancreatic tumor, usually occurring in young women, with solid and sometimes cystic or hemorrhagic components. Tumor cells may form solid sheets and pseudopapillary structures and often show nuclear beta-catenin expression.
symptoms_in_common: Well-defined pancreatic mass on CT
Solid cellular neoplasm on histology
Pancreatic-head-region lesion can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No patient age or sex was provided

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor showing acinar differentiation and production of pancreatic digestive enzymes. It often forms a large, well-demarcated solid pancreatic mass and may demonstrate acinar or sheet-like tumor architecture.

Highly cellular tumor on histology
Tumor cells may grow in sheets or acinar-like patterns
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain or weight loss was provided
No jaundice was provided
No lipase-hypersecretion syndrome, panniculitis, or polyarthritis was provided

Solid pancreatic lesion on CT

Diffuse cellular histologic appearance can mimic a lymphoid neoplasm
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats, or weight loss was provided

data.description: A benign vascular lesion within muscle or subcutaneous tissue, often containing dilated venous channels and phleboliths; it may appear as a slowly enlarging soft-tissue mass with increased uptake on blood-pool or nuclear imaging.

Bluish or bruised discoloration of the overlying skin
CT appearance of a vascular soft-tissue lesion with calcified phlebolith-like foci
Prominent vascular structures on three-dimensional CT angiographic imaging
Focal radionuclide uptake corresponding to the lesion

data.diagnosis: Arteriovenous malformation of the pelvis or gluteal region
data.description: An abnormal direct communication between arteries and veins that produces a high-flow vascular nidus, enlarged feeding arteries, and early draining veins. It can cause a visible or palpable mass and superficial skin color changes.

Overlying bluish-purple discoloration
Prominent feeding or draining vessels on angiographic reconstruction
Focal increased activity on radionuclide imaging

data.description: A benign lesion composed of large dilated blood-filled vascular spaces, often occurring in skeletal muscle or subcutaneous tissue and sometimes associated with phleboliths and chronic skin discoloration.

Possible chronic bluish or ecchymotic skin appearance
Lobulated vascular lesion on CT
Calcifications compatible with phleboliths
Focal uptake on nuclear imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent prominent arterial vascular anatomy may suggest an arteriovenous component rather than an isolated cavernous hemangioma

Bruise-like or violaceous skin discoloration
Potentially vascular appearance on contrast imaging
